question: What claim is made about the functions attributed in this address to the fortunate and beloved one?
premises: Killing and uprooting are attributed here.
Paralyzing, deluding, and what follows are attributed here.
Both sets are addressed to the same fortunate and beloved one.
inference: Killing, uprooting, paralyzing, deluding, and the like are the functions in view here.
uncertainties: The agent by whom these functions are carried out is not specified in this verse.
plain_english: Killing and uprooting, O fortunate one, and paralyzing, deluding, and so forth, O beloved one.
